playbook:
- Nerfs (lower damage or stats, higher cooldowns or mana costs) make pros pick a hero less: predict "down".
- Buffs make pros pick a hero more: predict "up".
- Mixed or small changes: predict "flat".

text:
- Nerfs (lower damage or stats, higher cooldowns or mana costs) to a hero's core abilities make pros pick it less: predict "down". Buffs to core abilities make pros pick it more: predict "up".
- Talent swaps, talent number tweaks, minor numeric tweaks, and quality-of-life or text changes are noise, so don't treat them as real buffs or nerfs. If a patch has only these, judge by prior popularity (see next rule) instead of defaulting to "flat".
- Use prior popularity as the main tiebreaker for small or mixed changes. Heroes in the most-picked third (>10%) usually fall ("down") after almost any patch that trims them, mixes buffs and nerfs, or removes a facet or utility. Regression to the mean is strong at the top. Heroes in the least-picked third (<=4.5%) usually rise ("up") after any non-trivial buff or neutral rework, since they have room to grow. Middle-popularity heroes are split, so follow the net direction of the core ability changes.
- Base attribute or stat reworks matter more than they look. A hero that gets a large base damage jump but a much lower per-level damage gain, or that switches primary attribute, is really getting a late-game nerf. The result is a big pick-rate drop for popular carries and a possible rise for low-pick heroes that gain early power or a better attribute.
- Predict "flat" only when the changes are tiny and the hero is mid or low in popularity. Flat is rare (about 15% of cases), so with any substantive change lean to up or down rather than flat.

text:
- Nerfs (lower damage or stats, higher cooldowns or mana costs) to a hero's core abilities make pros pick it less: predict "down". Buffs to core abilities make pros pick it more: predict "up".
- Talent swaps, talent number tweaks, minor numeric tweaks, and quality-of-life or text changes are noise, so don't treat them as real buffs or nerfs. If a patch has only these, judge by prior popularity (see next rule) instead of defaulting to "flat". Very small changes on a mid or low-popularity hero (a couple of talent tweaks, a lifesteal-rule or text change, one minor number) are often truly "flat".
- Use prior popularity as the main tiebreaker for small or mixed changes. Heroes in the most-picked third (>10%) often fall ("down") after trims, mixed changes, or removed facets, but not when they get real base stat or damage gains: then predict "up" or hold. Heroes in the least-picked third (<=4.5%) rise after a clear buff to core abilities, but don't assume "up" from noise-level changes alone. Middle-popularity heroes are split, so follow the net direction of the core ability changes.
- The 7.36-style base attribute rework (large "Base Damage increased", lower "Damage gain per level", and higher stat gains) is NOT a reliable signal. Judge it by the early-game picture. If level-1 damage rises or stays the same and stat gains rise, treat it as a mild buff for mid and top heroes: predict "up", or "flat" when the hero is low-pick. Predict "down" only if level-1 damage is unchanged and the level-30 drop is large, or the hero is low-pick and switches attribute. Low-pick heroes with a big late-game loss usually fall further.
- Removing a facet is not by itself a nerf. Treat it as neutral unless the hero's core ability was also cut.
- Predict "flat" when the changes are tiny and the hero is mid or low in popularity. Flat is rare (about 15% of cases), so with any substantive change lean to up or down.

- Nerfs (lower damage or stats, higher cooldowns or mana costs) to a hero's core abilities make pros pick it less: predict "down". Buffs to core abilities make pros pick it more: predict "up".
- Talent swaps, talent number tweaks, minor numeric tweaks, and quality-of-life or text changes are noise, so don't treat them as real buffs or nerfs. If a patch has only these, judge by prior popularity (see next rule) instead of defaulting to "flat". Very small changes on a mid or low-popularity hero (a couple of talent tweaks, a lifesteal-rule or text change, one minor number) are often truly "flat".
- Use prior popularity as the main tiebreaker for small or mixed changes. Heroes in the most-picked third (>10%) often fall ("down") after trims, mixed changes, or removed facets, but not when they get real base stat or damage gains: then predict "up" or hold. Heroes in the least-picked third (<=4.5%) rise after a clear buff to core abilities, but don't assume "up" from noise-level changes alone. Middle-popularity heroes are split, so follow the net direction of the core ability changes.
- The 7.36-style base attribute rework (large "Base Damage increased", lower "Damage gain per level", higher stat gains) is NOT a reliable signal. If level-1 damage rises or stays the same and stat gains rise, treat it as a mild buff for mid and top heroes ("up"), or "flat" for low-pick heroes. Predict "down" only if level-1 damage is unchanged and the level-30 drop is large, or the hero is low-pick and switches attribute. Low-pick heroes with a big late-game loss (≥35–50 damage) often fall further, even with a small ability buff, so don't call "up" for them.
- Removing a facet is not by itself a nerf. Treat it as neutral unless the hero's core ability was also cut.
- **Ability numeric buffs only count if they hit the hero's main pick reason (primary damage, stun, core spell).** Buffs limited to Aghanim's Shard/Scepter, secondary or situational spells, or accompanied by removed utility (e.g. no longer restores mana, no longer kills illusions, removed ability, cast-range or "affects only self" cuts) are net neutral or negative: don't predict "up" from them. A hero that loses a defining ability or mechanic, or has a mixed patch with a real nerf, leans "down" when it was popular or mid-pick.
- Predict "flat" when the changes are tiny and the hero is mid or low in popularity. Flat is rare (about 15% of cases), so with any substantive change lean to up or down. A hero with an all-talent patch that reshuffles many talents on a popular hero (>9%) leans "down" rather than "flat".

text:
- Nerfs (lower damage or stats, higher cooldowns or mana costs) to a hero's core abilities make pros pick it less: predict "down". Buffs to core abilities make pros pick it more: predict "up".
- Talent swaps, talent number tweaks, minor numeric tweaks, and quality-of-life or text changes are noise, so don't treat them as real buffs or nerfs. If a patch has only these, judge by prior popularity (see next rule) instead of defaulting to "flat". Very small changes on a mid or low-popularity hero (a couple of talent tweaks, a lifesteal-rule or text change, one minor number) are often truly "flat".
- **Popularity is the main tiebreaker for small or mixed changes, but top-third heroes (>10%) are not automatically "down".** Top-pick heroes with only talent swaps, removed facets, or trims to secondary abilities (slow duration, evasion, lifesteal-rule or creep-penalty changes) usually hold or rise, so predict "up" or hold. Predict "down" for them only when a core ability (main damage, stun, defining spell) is actually cut, or the hero loses a defining mechanic. Least-picked heroes (<=4.5%) rise after a clear buff to core abilities, and noise-only patches on them are "flat" (occasionally "up"). Middle-popularity heroes follow the net direction of the core ability changes.
- **The 7.36-style base attribute rework (large "Base Damage increased", lower "Damage gain per level", higher stat gains) is a mild buff, not a nerf.** If level-1 damage rises or stays the same and stat gains rise, predict "up" for mid and top heroes. For low-pick heroes predict "up" or "flat", not "down", even when level-30 damage falls by 45-60. A large level-30 drop only points "down" when level-1 damage is unchanged or lower and the hero is not top-pick. Switching to Universal with small stat or damage changes and no core ability buff is not a buff. Predict "flat" or "down" for low-pick heroes, especially if an ability is also nerfed.
- Removing a facet is not by itself a nerf. Treat it as neutral unless the hero's core ability was also cut.
- Ability numeric buffs only count if they hit the hero's main pick reason (primary damage, stun, core spell). Buffs limited to Aghanim's Shard/Scepter, secondary or situational spells, or accompanied by removed utility (no longer restores mana, removed ability, cast-range or "affects only self" cuts) are net neutral or negative: don't predict "up" from them. A hero that loses a defining ability or mechanic, or has a mixed patch with a real nerf to a core spell, leans "down" when it was mid-pick.
- Predict "flat" when the changes are tiny and the hero is mid or low in popularity. Flat is rare (about 15% of cases), so with any substantive change lean to up or down.

text:
- Nerfs (lower damage or stats, higher cooldowns or mana costs) to a hero's core abilities make pros pick it less: predict "down". Buffs to core abilities make pros pick it more: predict "up".
- Talent swaps, talent number tweaks, minor numeric tweaks, and quality-of-life or text changes are noise, so don't treat them as real buffs or nerfs. If a patch has only these, judge by prior popularity (see next rule) instead of defaulting to "flat". Very small changes on a mid or low-popularity hero (a couple of talent tweaks, a lifesteal-rule or text change, one minor number) are often truly "flat".
- Use prior popularity as the main tiebreaker for small or mixed changes. Heroes in the most-picked third (>10%) often fall ("down") after trims, mixed changes, or removed facets, but not when they get real base stat or damage gains: then predict "up" or hold. **Heroes at the very top (>15%) tend to regress even after modest numeric buffs to a core ability (small % bumps, cheaper mana, radius or damage nudges). Predict "down" for them unless the buff is large or adds a new mechanic.** Heroes in the least-picked third (<=4.5%) rise after a clear buff to core abilities, but don't assume "up" from noise-level changes alone. Middle-popularity heroes are split, so follow the net direction of the core ability changes.
- The 7.36-style base attribute rework (large "Base Damage increased", lower "Damage gain per level", higher stat gains) is NOT a reliable signal. If level-1 damage rises or stays the same and stat gains rise, treat it as a mild buff for mid and top heroes ("up"), or "flat" for low-pick heroes. Predict "down" only if level-1 damage is unchanged and the level-30 drop is large, or the hero is low-pick and switches attribute. Low-pick heroes with a big late-game loss (≥35–50 damage) often fall further, even with a small ability buff, so don't call "up" for them.
- Removing a facet is not by itself a nerf. Treat it as neutral unless the hero's core ability was also cut. **For low and mid-pick heroes (<10%), a patch of only removed facets and talent swaps or buffs leans "up", not "flat": the hero keeps its kit and often gains from the free slot or the buffed talents.**
- **Ability numeric buffs only count if they hit the hero's main pick reason (primary damage, stun, core spell).** Buffs limited to Aghanim's Shard/Scepter, secondary or situational spells, or accompanied by removed utility (e.g. no longer restores mana, no longer kills illusions, removed ability, cast-range or "affects only self" cuts) are net neutral or negative: don't predict "up" from them. **Patches that only rework or shuffle Shard/Scepter effects (dispel changes, pull-to-slow swaps, reclassified damage) on low or mid heroes lean "down", not "flat".** A hero that loses a defining ability or mechanic, or has a mixed patch with a real nerf, leans "down" when it was popular or mid-pick.
- Predict "flat" when the changes are tiny and the hero is mid or low in popularity. Flat is rare (about 15% of cases), so with any substantive change lean to up or down. A hero with an all-talent patch that reshuffles many talents on a popular hero (>9%) leans "down" rather than "flat".

text:
- Nerfs (lower damage or stats, higher cooldowns or mana costs) to a hero's core abilities make pros pick it less: predict "down". Buffs to core abilities make pros pick it more: predict "up".
- Talent swaps, talent number tweaks, minor numeric tweaks, and quality-of-life or text changes are not real buffs or nerfs. **For a low or mid-pick hero (<=8%) with no core-ability nerf, a patch of talent swaps, talent buffs, small secondary-ability tweaks or removed facets leans "up", because these heroes tend to drift upward. Reserve "flat" for patches that are truly only text or QoL, or one lone minor number.**
- Use prior popularity as the main tiebreaker for small or mixed changes. Heroes in the most-picked third (>10%) often fall ("down") after trims, mixed changes, or removed facets, but not when they get real base stat or damage gains: then predict "up" or hold. Heroes in the least-picked third (<=4.5%) rise after a clear buff to core abilities. Middle-popularity heroes are split, so follow the net direction of the core ability changes.
- **The 7.36-style base attribute rework (large "Base Damage increased", lower "Damage gain per level", higher stat gains) is usually a mild buff, whatever the level-30 damage drop.** If level-1 damage rises or stays the same and stat gains rise, predict "up" for low, mid and top heroes. Hold at "flat" only when the stat gains are tiny or an ability is also nerfed. Predict "down" only if level-1 damage falls or is unchanged and the hero is mid or low-pick, or if the same patch also cuts a core ability.
- Removing a facet is not by itself a nerf. Treat it as neutral unless the hero's core ability was also cut.
- Ability numeric buffs only count if they hit the hero's main pick reason (primary damage, stun, core spell). Buffs limited to Aghanim's Shard/Scepter, secondary or situational spells, or accompanied by removed utility (e.g. no longer restores mana, no longer kills illusions, removed ability, cast-range or "affects only self" cuts) are net neutral or negative: don't predict "up" from them. A hero that loses a defining ability or mechanic, or has a mixed patch with a real nerf, leans "down" when it was popular or mid-pick.
- Predict "flat" only when the changes are tiny and the hero is mid or low in popularity. Flat is rare (about 15% of cases), so with any substantive change lean to up or down. A hero with an all-talent patch that reshuffles many talents on a popular hero (>9%) leans "down" rather than "flat".
